Load required libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(measurements)

# Problem 1

Importing the NY NOAA data set from the p8105 library.

```{r}
library(p8105.datasets)
data("ny_noaa")
```

The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Association data set contains weather data that are available from weather stations globally. The NY NOAA data set contains **`r nrow(ny_noaa)`** observations and **`r ncol(ny_noaa)`** variables. Variables include
**`r names(ny_noaa)`**. The data are collected from **`r min(ny_noaa$date)`** to **`r max(ny_noaa$date)`**. ID refers to the weather station ID from which data are collected. The range of values of precipitation is **`r range(ny_noaa$prcp, na.rm = TRUE)`**  (tenths of mm). The range of values of snowfall is **`r range(ny_noaa$snow, na.rm = TRUE)`** (mm). The range of values of snowdepth is **`r range(ny_noaa$snwd, na.rm = TRUE)`** (mm). The average maximum temperature is **`r round(mean(as.numeric(ny_noaa$tmax), na.rm = TRUE),1)`** (tenths of degrees C). The average minimum temperature is **`r round(mean(as.numeric(ny_noaa$tmin), na.rm = TRUE),1)`** (tenths of degrees C). 

## Further data cleaning, description and plotting 

- Creating separate variables for year, month, and day. 

```{r}

ny_noaa = ny_noaa %>%
  mutate(
  year = year(date),
  month = month(date),
  day = day(date)
)
```


- Giving observations for temperature, precipitation, and snowfall reasonable units. 

    Changing temperature variables to Fahrenheit, prcipitation and snowfall to inches. 
    
```{r}
ny_noaa = ny_noaa %>%
  mutate(
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax),
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin),
    prcp = prcp / 254,
    snow = snow / 25.4,
    snwd = snwd / 25.4,
    tmax = conv_unit(tmax / 10, "C", "F"),
    tmin = conv_unit(tmin / 10, "C", "F")
  )
```
    
- For snowfall, what are the most commonly observed values? Why?

  The most commonly observed snowfall value is **`r names(which.max(table(ny_noaa$snow)))`** inches. Snowfall is seasonal in New York, thus    commonly there is no snow. 

- Two-panel plot showing the average max temperature in January and in July in each station across years. 

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
ny_noaa %>%
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) %>%
  group_by(id, year, month) %>%
  summarize(mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(. ~ month) +
  labs(
    title = "Average maximum temperature by station, January and July",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Mean max temperature (F)"
  )
```


- Is there any observable / interpretable structure? Any outliers?
  
  Average temperature appears to be increasing slightly in January since 1980. There is yearly fluctuation in average temperature. There       appears to be one major outlier in 1988 for average temp in July at one station. 


- Two-panel plot showing tmax vs tmin for the full dataset (note that a scatterplot may not be the best option)
```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
ny_noaa %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(tmax, tmin),
    names_to = "min_max",
    values_to = "temp"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = temp)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
  facet_grid(. ~ min_max) +
  labs(
    title = "Maximum and minimum temperature",
    x = "Temperature (F)",
    y = "Count"
  )
```


- Plot showing the distribution of snowfall values greater than 0 and less than 100 separately by year.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
ny_noaa %>%
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = snow, group = year)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Snowfall (mm)")

```

# Problem 2


Loading NHANES data - accelerometer and demographic data 

```{r,  echo=TRUE, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE }
nhanes_accel <- read_csv("data/nhanes_accel.csv")

nhanes_covar <- read_csv("data/nhanes_covar.csv", skip = 4)
```

Tidy Accelerometer data

```{r}
nhanes_accel_long =
  nhanes_accel %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("min"),
    names_to = "min",
    names_prefix = "min",
    values_to = "accel") %>%
         mutate(min = as.integer(min))
      
```

Merge and filter data sets: 

- Exclude participants less than 21 years of age, and those with missing demographic data; and encode data with reasonable variable classes

```{r,  echo=TRUE, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE }
nhanes <- nhanes_covar %>%
  filter(age >= 21, complete.cases(sex, age, BMI, education)) %>%
  left_join(nhanes_accel_long, by = "SEQN") %>%
  mutate(sex = factor(sex, labels = c("male", "female")),
        education = factor(education, labels = c("<high school", "high school ", ">high school")))
  
```

- Number of men and women in each education category

```{r}
nhanes %>%
  distinct(SEQN, sex, education) %>%
  count(sex, education) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = education, values_from = n) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Number of men and women by education category")

```

- Visualization of the age distributions for men and women in each education category.

```{r}
nhanes %>%
  distinct(SEQN, sex, education, age) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = education, y = age)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_grid(~ sex) +
  labs(x = "Education", y = "Age")
```

- Those with more than a high school education are the most numerous in the sample. Educational categories are fairly evently distributed by   sex. Those with more than a high school education tend to be younger in age in the sample data. 


Plotting total activity by age - including sex and education 

```{r, message= FALSE}
#Creating variable for total activity for unique SEQN
nhanes %>%
  mutate(total_act = sum(accel, na.rm = TRUE), .by = SEQN)%>%
  group_by(sex, education) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = total_act, color = sex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(. ~ education) +
  labs(
    title = "Total Physical Activity by Age",
    x = "Age",
    y = "Total Physical Activity"
  )
  
```

- The total activity of participants generally decreases with age. Younger individuals with less than a high school education appear to be   more physically active than other groups. Women appear, on average, to be more physically active than men. 


Plotting activity throughout the day: 

```{r, message= FALSE}

nhanes %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = min, y = accel, color = sex)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = SEQN), alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(. ~ education) +
  labs(
    title = "Physical Activity throughout the day",
    x = "time",
    y = "Physical Activity"
  )
```

 - There appears to be more variation in physical activity throughout the day in men and women with greater than a high school education. Activity generally peaks for all groups mid morning, and remains level through the evening. Women in the sample appear slightly more physically active than the men. 

# Problem 3

Importing Citi bike Data & Merging. Creating variable for month and year

```{r,  echo=TRUE, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE }
citi_jan20 <- read_csv("data/citi/Jan 2020 Citi.csv") %>%
  mutate(month = "January", year = 2020)

citi_jan24 <- read_csv("data/citi/Jan 2024 Citi.csv") %>%
  mutate(month = "January", year = 2024)

citi_jul20 <- read_csv("data/citi/July 2020 Citi.csv") %>%
  mutate(month = "July", year = 2020)

citi_jul24 <- read_csv("data/citi/July 2024 Citi.csv") %>%
  mutate(month = "July", year = 2024)

citi_all <- bind_rows(citi_jan20, citi_jan24, citi_jul20, citi_jul24)
```

The Citi Bike combined data contains **`r nrow(citi_all)`** rides and **`r ncol(citi_all)`** variables. Variables included are the ride ID, the type of ride: Classic or Ebike, day of the week, duration of the ride, the station the ride started in, the station the ride ended in, the membership type, month, and year. The average duration of the rides included in the data set is **`r mean(citi_all$duration, na.rm = TRUE)`** minutes. There were **`r sum(citi_all$member_casual == "member")`** member rides and **`r sum(citi_all$member_casual == "casual")`** casual rides. There were **`r sum(citi_all$rideable_type == "classic_bike")`** classic rides and **`r sum(citi_all$rideable_type == "electric_bike")`** electric rides.


Total number of rides in each combination of year and month separating casual riders and Citi Bike members. 

```{r}

citi_all %>%
  group_by(member_casual)%>%
  count(year, month) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = member_casual, values_from = n) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Rides by Membership Type")
```

- Overall casual rides have increased dramatically between 2020 and 2024. Ride usage increased in both years from january to july, likely due to weather. Casual rides increased more seasonally than did the membership rides. 

Table showing the 5 most popular starting stations for July 2024; include the number of rides originating from these stations.

```{r}
citi_all %>%
  filter(year == 2024, month == "July") %>%
  count(start_station_name, sort = TRUE) %>%
  head(5) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Top 5 starting stations, July 2024")

```
